title: Compile-Time Constants
goal: Declare global constants with const and know when to use static.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Afternoon: User-Defined Types

sections.text: You use constants in C++ or Java to give fixed values names across your program.

sections.caption: const requires an explicit type annotation.

sections.text: Values marked const are evaluated at compile time and inlined wherever they are used. They have no fixed memory address.

sections.caption: static has a fixed location in memory.

sections.text: Use static when you need object identity or a fixed location in memory. Otherwise, preferred practice is const.

sections.caption: const fn can execute at compile time.

sections.text: Omitting type annotations on const or static is a compiler error because global types are never inferred.

explanation: Declare global constants with const and know when to use static.
